verified.exploit_entry_point: Template selection by name through the real public API: new Handlebars(loader).compile(name) / loader.sourceAt(name), template partial references, and a Spring MVC controller view name resolved by the view resolver. At the pinned (+injected) commit a crafted name reads a resource outside the configured template location or of a different suffix; the behavioural signal is 'an out-of-bounds marker resource was read' vs 'the name was refused with a client error and nothing out of bounds was read'. The Spring ResourceLoader / ServletContext collaborators are stubbed to answer like the real infrastructure (the attacker-controlled input is the name).
sites: SpringTemplateLoader.getResource/resolve: suffix truncation via a URL fragment/query in the resolved location, caller-supplied protocol preserved, and no prefix boundary (reported sink + its traversal check)
HandlebarsViewResolver.configure: unsafe controller view name (protocol/fragment/traversal) rejected before compilation (far site, web layer)
injected_siblings: S1 FileTemplateLoader: a resolve()/getResource override that treats a caller-supplied 'file:' name as an absolute URL, bypassing the base-directory boundary and the suffix (added by inject-siblings.patch)

S2 ServletContextTemplateLoader: a leading-slash 'absolute context path' fast-path that skips the normalise+boundary step, allowing relative traversal out of the prefix (added by inject-siblings.patch)
verified.uncovered_routes_pattern_B: Screener lead SpringTemplateLoader missing validatePrefixSuffix (root-prefix + empty-suffix guard) verified: it is developer-configuration driven (prefix/suffix are set by the integrator, not attacker input), is not the advisory's fragment/boundary flaw, and is not reachable from any attacker-supplied name. Dismissed, not built; registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv. The pattern-B role is filled by the injected sibling loaders in the core module, which the published Spring-MVC-only fix never touches.
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own Spring MVC loader test (SpringTemplateLoaderTest) is compiled and run online during the image build to warm the offline Maven cache, and is shipped (re-expressed) as a functional test. The graded hidden suite runs offline via Maven surefire. On the pinned+injected code all 8 security test cases fail and all 7 functional test cases pass; on the oracle all pass.

traps.shape: reported sink: a resolved template location whose trailing characters (a '#' fragment or '?' query) make a URL-backed resource load ignore the configured suffix, reading a resource of a different type
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none needed - this is the class and behaviour the report points at; the obvious lever

traps.shape: far (same sink, different shape): a relative-traversal name climbs out of the configured prefix; a fragment-only fix misses it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a solver who blocks the fragment/query suffix trick may assume relative traversal is already handled by the resource layer's path normalisation

traps.shape: far site in another file (web layer): a controller view name carrying a protocol, fragment or traversal must be rejected before it is compiled
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a web-layer wrapper that looks redundant once the loader is hardened, and out of scope relative to the reported loader

traps.shape: injected sibling (core module): a file-system loader treats a caller-supplied 'file:' name as an absolute URL and loads it directly, bypassing the base-directory boundary and the suffix
traps.where: handlebars/src/main/java/com/github/jknack/handlebars/io/FileTemplateLoader.java (resolve + getResource file: branch, added by inject-siblings.patch)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: URI-style template names look like an unsupported / neighbouring feature that only triggers for a 'file:'-prefixed name, easy to skip while hardening the Spring loader
traps.realistic_because: the Spring loader already keeps a caller-supplied 'file:'/'classpath:' protocol at the front of the location; a maintainer adding the documented 'file:C:/page.html' style name support to the file loader would copy that shape. INJECTED into our copy only; registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

traps.shape: injected sibling (core module): a servlet-context loader passes 'absolute' context-path names straight to the container, skipping the normalise + boundary step, so relative traversal escapes the prefix
traps.reason_to_dismiss: reads as a legacy/compat path for webapp-absolute includes that the container is trusted to resolve - an internal/trusted-caller assumption
traps.realistic_because: servlet containers resolve resources relative to the web-application root and many do not normalise '..'; the loader normally normalises/bounds the path itself, and a maintainer could plausibly decide to trust absolute context paths. INJECTED into our copy only; registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a fix that throws on every load still throws on the legitimate positive-control functional loads (nested names, protocol-qualified prefixes, 'template'), so it fails functionally; there is no crash-as-refusal that passes
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is a single protected operation (reading the template resource a name resolves to); there is no neighbouring or proxy resource a fix could authorise or read by mistake
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: template resolution has no roles, peers or directions; every entry point and every backing loader is the same read, and the suite drives each of them
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: template loading is inherently a read; there is no write/other-verb subset a fix could guard while leaving reads open
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the boundary and suffix guards operate on the resolved location before the resource is fetched; the normalisation only ever narrows what is accepted (an unsafe name is rejected, never repaired into a safe one), so there is no adjust-then-check ordering a fix could get wrong and still pass
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity, principal or credential string is parsed on the protected path; the decision is a path/URL boundary, so a malformed spelling cannot make a guard see an empty subject
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the boundary decision is computed locally from the configured location and the name; there is no external authority that could return empty and cause a fail-open
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the fix adds per-loader guards and (in the oracle) removes the injected overrides; it does not change the stated behaviour of a shared helper a sibling relies on. The alt_fix pass patch reimplements the URL-component guard and keeps every functional contract

notes: Injected track, pattern A+B. inject-siblings.patch (in environment/) adds the two sibling loader gaps (FileTemplateLoader, ServletContextTemplateLoader) to our copy only, applied at image build after checkout. Oracle = published Spring MVC fix (SpringTemplateLoader boundary + URL-component validation + protocol-preservation removal; HandlebarsViewResolver view-name rejection) plus removal of the two injected sibling gaps. The screener's pattern-B lead (missing validatePrefixSuffix on the Spring loader) was verified developer-configuration-driven and not attacker-reachable; dismissed and registered.
